content.what_it_is: MATLAB postprocessor copied from the ETA_Liner pattern: it loads four eta snapshots (L6-L14), extracts row 2, creates a normalized coordinate from the first file's length (L20-L23), filters -10<=x<=20 and normalizes four amplitude columns (L25-L37), reconstructs the coordinate column (L38-L42), and writes a five-column table (L44).
entities: fdir @L2; dep @L4; d @L6; n @L7; d1 @L8; d2 @L10; d3 @L12; d4 @L14
dx @L20; loop index i @L21; x @L22; ii @L25; kk @L30; data @L31; ll @L38

equations.ref: first normalized eta column; columns 3-5 repeat for d2-d4
coordinate column reordered to match reverse selection

unresolved: Copied cross-file range defect across L7-L14 and L31-L34: n comes only from eta_0085 but indexes d1-d4 without checking that every file has row 2 and n columns; a shorter/differently shaped snapshot overruns.
Copied empty-selection defect across L25-L44: when no x falls in [-10,20], kk and data remain undefined but the reconstruction/output still uses them.
length(d) at L7 chooses the largest dimension rather than the width of row 2, so a tall matrix can make d1(i) exceed its columns.
Equal file lengths are insufficient because the four inputs are never checked for a common spatial grid; columns can be silently misregistered.
